payout_quote: Poplin's own press release (Business Wire): 'Laundry Pros set their own hours... and keep a 75% share of every job and 100% of tips.' Reported platform terms (TMJ4, quoting Poplin): 'Sudsters are paid $0.75 per pound for next-day delivery or $1.50 per pound for same-day delivery, plus tips and bonuses... you'll always make at least $15 (plus tips) per order... You can receive a payment within two days.'
timing: Payment within two days of order (reported platform terms).
eligibility: Access to a washer, dryer, and air-drying setup
steps: Register as a Poplin Laundry Pro and pass the background check
Set your service radius in the app
Accept orders: pick up laundry from customers
Wash, dry, fold, and return within the service window
Get paid $0.75/lb ($1.50/lb same-day) + 100% tips, within ~2 days
catches: You pay for detergent, water, electricity, gas, and laundromat runs — margins are thinner than the per-pound rate suggests
Minimum $15/order is guaranteed but heavy lifting comes from volume
Same-day $1.50/lb pays double but demands same-day turnaround
Poplin keeps 25% of the job value (you keep 75% + all tips)
Your home becomes a laundromat — space and machine wear are real costs
biggest_catch: The $0.75/lb rate is gross — detergent, water, power, gas, and machine wear come out of your pocket, and you need serious volume (15+ loads a day like top earners) to make real money.
upfront_fee: $0 signup; washer/dryer, supplies, and transport are worker-provided.

weasel_words.quote: 'Top earners... can make thousands per month' — outliers working 15 loads/day, not typical results.

repeatable.cadence: Accept an order, pick it up, wash-dry-fold-return it in the service window, and get paid within two days — stack multiple customers' loads per cycle to make the loop profitable.

maximize: Take same-day $1.50/lb orders whenever offered — double pay for the same load; stack multiple customers' loads in one wash cycle to multiply per-pound revenue against fixed machine time; set a tight pickup radius to cut gas; use a laundromat's big machines on high-volume days to clear more pounds per hour; upsell hang-dry/delicates if the app supports add-ons; track detergent, power, and mileage as deductions.
who_pays: Poplin pays you — you keep a 75% share of every job plus 100% of tips, and Poplin processes payment within about two days. The customer pays the platform; Poplin passes your share to you.
who_qualifies: You need access to a washer and dryer (plus an air-drying setup), your own detergent and supplies, transportation for pickup and delivery, a bathroom scale and bags, and you must pass a background check that requires your SSN.
work_available: Orders come through the app and the real money is in volume — top earners do 15+ loads a day. Per-order minimums are small ($15), so this is a volume game, and availability varies by market.
what_gets_accepted: You get paid for each completed order — picked up, washed, dried, folded, and returned in the service window — and customers rate and tip you in the app after delivery. One hard rule from Poplin's own help center: never accept tips off-platform (cash, Venmo, PayPal) — it's against company policy and can get your account deactivated. Broader removal criteria are not publicly stated.
costs_and_unpaid_time: Signup is officially free. Everything operational is on you: detergent, water, electricity, gas, laundromat runs, and wear on your machines — these eat the per-pound rate fast. Unpaid time: registration and the background check, driving pickups and deliveries, and the sorting and folding time folded into the flat per-pound rate.
when_cash_arrives: Payment within two days of the order, per Poplin's reported platform terms.
